Race-pace segments on pre-fatigued legs: Race-pace segments on pre-fatigued legs rehearse race-specific economy and pacing, while the easy running around them keeps the session aerobic and recovery manageable. Keep the easy parts truly easy so the fast parts are controlled and even.
Repeatable, controlled threshold work wi: Repeatable, controlled threshold work with easy recoveries. Pace is a provisional ceiling, not a target to beat; reduce effort for rising HR, lactate, breathing or fatigue.
Short fast reps near VO2max pace recruit: Short fast reps near VO2max pace recruit fast-twitch fibres and sharpen running economy and neuromuscular speed; brief jog recoveries let you repeat quality without lactate build-up. Keep the last rep as fast as the first.
Reps at roughly 5-10K pace accumulate ti: Reps at roughly 5-10K pace accumulate time close to VO2max, the strongest stimulus for aerobic power, while jog recoveries clear lactate so each rep stays quality. Hold the last rep as controlled as the first.
Cruise intervals (Daniels) accumulate mo: Cruise intervals (Daniels) accumulate more time at lactate-threshold pace than a single run could, with short jog recoveries to limit fatigue. This raises the pace you can sustain before blood lactate climbs steeply.
Progressive blocks climb from just below: Progressive blocks climb from just below to threshold pace, training lactate clearance as fatigue accumulates and rehearsing negative-split pacing. Each block should feel controlled, not raced.
Descending blocks step from just slower: Descending blocks step from just slower than threshold toward 10K pace as they shorten, training threshold endurance and the ability to change gear on tired legs without extra load.
Over/unders alternate efforts just above: Over/unders alternate efforts just above threshold with floats at marathon pace and no stopping, so you produce lactate and clear it while still running. This trains lactate clearance and the ability to recover mid-race.
A sustained run at lactate-threshold pac: A sustained run at lactate-threshold pace, about the effort you could hold for an hour, improves lactate clearance and the fraction of VO2max you can sustain. Stay even and finish without sprinting.
Easy aerobic running, below the first la: Easy aerobic running, below the first lactate threshold, builds mitochondrial density, capillary supply and fat oxidation with little mechanical and hormonal stress, so the hard days can stay hard. If you can't talk in full sentences, slow down.
Race effort: starting at the slower end: Race effort: starting at the slower end of the target range conserves glycogen and delays lactate accumulation, and even pacing is the most economical way to cover the distance. Settle into rhythm before pushing.
